Definition: from G1909 and G2192; to hold upon, i.e. (by implication) to retain; (by extension) to detain; (with implication, of G3563) to pay attention to:--give (take) heed unto, hold forth, mark, stay.
BiblicalUsage: Epecho means to hold upon — to hold forth, to pay attention, to stay with something. Jesus marks how guests choose the chief rooms; the lame man gives heed to Peter and John, expecting to receive; Paul tells the Philippians to hold forth the word of life, and Timothy to take heed to himself and the doctrine.
TheologicalSignificance: Attention is faithfulness, and what we keep our eyes on shapes what we become. I hold that holding forth the word and holding fast to it are the same posture, and Timothy's charge is mine too: take heed to yourself and to the doctrine.
